semantic_changes: The leaderless interval is now derived from member State() samples rather than the cluster helper, so a short gap can be observed where the previous run reported none.
The target's own suffrage view is recorded before the transfer, which distinguishes a target that still believes it is a voter from one that already knows it is a non-voter.
Case names, admissions, assertions and case selection are unchanged; only the recorded fields differ.

scope.description: Two leadership-transfer invocations on real four-voter in-memory clusters, as before: the trigger demotes a non-leader member with DemoteVoter before LeadershipTransferToServer names it, the control leaves it a voter. Both now also read the target's own configuration view before the transfer and sample every member's State() every 10 ms for the watch window, recording candidate samples, leaderless samples and terms.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms).
The demotion call is completed and 200 ms elapse before the transfer; the harness records what the target itself believes rather than asserting convergence.
A leaderless sample means no member reported Leader at that instant; samples are 10 ms apart, so a shorter gap can still be missed.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about client requests accepted during the window and no safety claim about committed entries.
Transfers to members absent from the configuration entirely remain unexercised.

parameters.trigger_target: member demoted to non-voter before the transfer

basis.prefix: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with four bootstrapped voters, waits for c.Leader(), selects the first non-leader raft as target, and reads target.GetConfiguration() to record whether the target itself sees its suffrage as voter, nonvoter, absent or unknown. The trigger then calls leader.DemoteVoter(targetID, 0, 5s) and sleeps 200 ms; the control skips demotion. Both call leader.LeadershipTransferToServer(targetID, target.localAddr) and record the future's error and duration, then sample target.State() and every member's State() every 10 ms for five seconds, emitting future_ok, future_error, future_ms, target_ever_leader, final_leader_is_target, candidate_samples, leaderless_samples, no_leader_ms_sampled, samples, target_term_after and other_member_term_max_after.
basis.responsibility: The library owns target eligibility: it holds the latest configuration, its automatic path already excludes non-voters, and its documentation states that a follower which cannot be promoted will fail gracefully. A caller naming a configured member therefore relies on the library either to refuse an ineligible target or to report an outcome that matches what happened to authority.

comparisons.description: Control: a transfer to a voter must install that voter as leader.
Control: a transfer that installs the named voter must complete without error.
A transfer to a member the configuration marks as a non-voter cannot be promoted, so the documented graceful failure requires an error; a successful future contradicts it.
If the transfer is admitted as successful, the named target must hold leadership; a target that never leads contradicts the transfer's stated purpose.

before.description: Two leadership-transfer invocations on real four-voter in-memory clusters. In both, a non-leader member is chosen as the explicit target; in the trigger case that member is first demoted to non-voter through the public DemoteVoter API and the committed configuration is allowed to reach it, while the control keeps it a voter. Each case records the transfer future's outcome, whether the named target ever reported Leader, whether the final leader is the target, a sampled leaderless interval and the members' terms after the attempt.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms), so a new election can complete quickly.
The demotion is committed before the transfer is requested; the harness waits 200 ms and does not assert configuration convergence separately.

The leaderless interval is estimated from repeated 10 ms sampling whose measured effective rate was about one sample per 116 ms (43 samples), so a shorter leaderless gap can be missed and a zero count is not evidence of absence.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about the effect on client requests accepted during the transfer window, and no safety claim about committed entries.
Transfers to members absent from the configuration entirely (rejected earlier by the replState lookup) are not exercised.

responsibility.before: The library documents that a leadership transfer makes the target up to date, sends TimeoutNow, and that a follower which cannot be promoted will fail gracefully. Choosing which targets are admissible, and reporting an outcome that matches what happened to authority, are therefore library responsibilities: the caller supplies a member id that the configuration itself currently marks as a non-voter.
responsibility.after: The library owns target eligibility: it holds the latest configuration, its automatic path already excludes non-voters, and its documentation states that a follower which cannot be promoted will fail gracefully. A caller naming a configured member therefore relies on the library either to refuse an ineligible target or to report an outcome that matches what happened to authority.

revision_reason: Result events now also record candidate_samples and leaderless_samples sampled from each member's State(), and case events record target_role_in_own_config read from the target's own GetConfiguration future; the cluster-wide c.Leader() probe is no longer used inside the sampling loop, which raises the effective sample rate from about one per 116 ms to about one per 10 ms.
